title: Mixed record channels condition whole-name versus bound-field interpretation
summary: GDT735's historical observation separates descriptive learned-name records from prescriptive ingredient/quantity/process records. A bounded semantic question is whether the same Voynich construction changes interpretation when it occupies those channel types, rather than carrying one context-free word meaning.

design.mechanism: record-channel conditioning: a construction may be a learned whole/name in descriptive records but a bound field in prescriptive records
design.unit: complete repeated construction with independently coded record-channel and boundary role
design.contrast: channel-conditioned interpretation versus one invariant lexical meaning across descriptive and prescriptive records
design.prediction: After predeclaring channel markers, boundary behavior and neighboring slot types should separate the two interpretations; a held construction should not require the same argument/quantity behavior in both channels.
design.countermodel: The apparent channels may be editorial labels or a single fixed template whose neighbors vary freely; one invariant meaning can then produce both record profiles.
design.falsifier: On a held set with independently coded channel and boundary markers, the construction shows no channel-conditioned difference and the invariant-meaning model predicts all observed slot behavior equally well.
design.principal_risk: GDT735 is a historical architecture observation, not Voynich semantic gold; channel markers and independent whole-name/field annotations are currently unavailable.
design.related: Near GDT735, GDT744, and GDT775 historical channel work, but the proposed discriminator is conditional channel dependence of one construction, not a new head lexeme or generic decoder fit.

source_evidence.quote:
Die historische Brücke ist real, aber sie liegt **eine Ebene höher als ein
Wörterbuchgleichnis**. Spätmittelalterliche pharmazeutische Handschriften
belegen zwei komplementäre Recordtypen:

1. **deskriptiv:** gelernter Drogenname oder Lemma, optional Pflanzenteil oder
   Stoffform, Qualität/Zustand und Grad;
2. **präskriptiv:** Befehl, benannte Zutat oder Zubereitung, gebundene Menge,
   Einheit und Prozess/Produkt.

Der beste historische Arbeitsrahmen ist deshalb ein gemischtes System aus
gelernten Ganzformen und gebundenen Fachfeldern, das beide Recordtypen getrennt
hält. Das ist eine bessere Architektur als ein flaches Wort-für-Wort-Lexikon.

design.smallest_next_step: Source-review existing complete construction cards for independently recorded channel and boundary markers; stop if those markers are inherited renderer labels rather than observations.
